children: , the electric-vehicle and energy-infrastructure company, signed on as the charging operator for Forum Mobility's next three California freight depots Thursday, extending its charging technology deeper into commercial trucking. Shares gained nearly 2% to $364.43. The valuation snapshot shows the stock trading 9.15% above its $333.88 GF Value, putting investors at a clear premium to the GuruFocus estimate.

The new sites across northern and southern California will bring a combined 30 megawatts of heavy-duty truck charging capacity. The depots will pair Tesla's Megawatt Charging System with CCS connections and pull-through charging lanes designed for large commercial vehicles. Spread evenly, that headline capacity would work out to roughly 10 megawatts per depot, though Forum Mobility has not disclosed how the capacity will actually be divided among the three locations.

The key point is infrastructure, not an implied rush of Semi sales. Thirty megawatts of new charging capacity removes one of the practical bottlenecks facing fleets considering electric heavy trucks: finding fast, accessible charging away from their own yards. Tesla also gets another avenue to monetize its charging ecosystem beyond passenger vehicles. What remains unknown is just as importantForum disclosed no vehicle-order commitment, utilization target or economics for Tesla's operating contract, leaving the financial contribution unclear even as the network footprint expands.

title: Tesla Jumps 2% as 30 Megawatts Build a Semi Beachhead
